title: Scan store: folder totals, hardlinks counted once, children largest first
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: Each folder's rolled-up size and rolled-up on-disk size equal the sums over every file below it, at any depth (10,000-deep chain, very wide, empty, mixed trees vs brute force): missing

When several names share one 128-bit file ID, the first name seen charges the bytes; later names count as files and add 0 bytes (unit test: one ID under three names in three folders; root total equals one copy, only the first name's folder is charged): partial
Each folder records how many files are below it, counting every name of a hardlinked file (asserted at every level in the hardlink test): missing

A link entry, or a folder that could not be opened, stays in the tree as a leaf that adds no bytes and has nothing below it (unit test with non-zero stated sizes; parent's totals unchanged; no children): partial

A folder's children can be read largest first by on-disk size, each with its share of the parent; a 0-byte parent gives every child a 0 share, not an error (tests: ordering, equal sizes stable, hand-computed shares, 0-byte parent): missing
Reading the ordered children of a folder with 100,000 children takes under 0.25 s (timed test in a release build over 10 reads on a synthetic store): missing
first-seen-charging-repeatable: 16-worker first-seen: 68 folders swing >10 MiB in 5 runs (WinSxS 587 MiB); control moved 0 B

Should scan-wide Totals and --report stop counting a folder's own allocation (a big directory's index)? This design says yes, per criteria 1 and 4. It changes reported totals only where a directory lists a non-zero size. If the person wants that space shown, it needs its own column, not RolledOnDisk.

Criterion 2's 'first name seen charges the bytes' is repeatable only with one writer thread and a fixed append order (spike: no-go with 16 workers). U-012 says per-file queries are 5x slower than listing, so a parallel scanner is likely later. Should that future slice serialize appends deterministically, or should criterion 2 be re-agreed as per-subtree counting, which lets children sum to more than their parent?
Sort-on-read with no stored order departs from the architecture line that the store holds children sorted largest first. A reviewer may prefer a cached or stored order.
Rollup columns sit on every row (simple, 95 MiB) rather than a folder-slot layout (about 30 MiB, an extra indirection). A reviewer may prefer the smaller one up front.
I dropped the proposal's share clamp and its JIT-optimised guard on the timing test. The proposal kept both as defensive measures.
New store reads live in a partial-class file ScanStore.Rollup.cs, a boundary chosen to shrink the SL-040 merge surface. A reviewer may prefer them inline or in a separate type.
The oracle is split into Expected(model) and CheckStructure(store). A reviewer may want a single helper.

A real-NTFS test that a folder's own directory allocation is in no total (C-008, second half). The m7 probe with the project's DirectoryReader found local NTFS lists every folder at EndOfFile 0 and AllocationSize 0: a 1,500-name folder, plus all 356 folders listed in C:\, C:\Windows, C:\Windows\System32 and C:\Program Files. Such a test could not fail before the change. The synthetic 4096/4096 case stands in, as the m7 disposition directs.
The Scan Store line in the engine's own architecture record is not edited: that record is not in this worktree. The revised line is written in docs/design/SL-042-folder-totals.md.

Edit the Scan Store line in the engine's architecture record to: 'children are ordered largest first on read (ChildrenLargestFirst); no order is stored unless criterion 6's timing test fails'. This is the m9 revision. It is written in docs/design/SL-042-folder-totals.md, but the engine's record is outside this worktree. It should wait until the person answers the design's open question on sort-on-read versus a stored order.

The open question on Totals and folders' own allocation now has data: local NTFS lists every folder at 0 bytes (probe output in the doc), so dropping them changes nothing locally and only matters where a listing gives folders a size, such as SMB.

Whichever of SL-040 and SL-042 merges second must follow the merge note in docs/design/SL-042-folder-totals.md: grep its tests for TryAddFileId and HardlinkDuplicate and rebuild those duplicates by appending a repeated ID. It must also append parents before children and never under a file, a link or an Unreadable folder.

A future parallel Scanner must keep a single writer thread and a deterministic append order, or criterion 2 must be re-agreed (open design question). Nothing enforces this at run time; M3 was overridden.

TopLevelTracker is now a second accumulator of numbers the store owns, pinned to the rollups by the real-tree assertions. The tree slice can retire it and delete the SL-039 'window never touches the scan store' rule on purpose.

Pre-existing, seen with the trunk exe as well: at the ending, the window's CountersText shows a progress sample behind the final totals. On C:\Windows it read 184,376 files against a final 188,532, while OutcomeDetail shows the final figures. Not changed by this slice.
